what: The drift between tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py's derivation and the committed letter-list cards, in the keys and the membership the mint OWNS (KEY_OWNERS in that file), as it stood on 2026-10-04 when --check was first gated on it. Each row is a reading still owed, and names the ticket that owes it: T-2071 the households the mint no longer derives and the ones it re-mints under a new id, T-2072 the people it would add, T-2073 the cards whose mint-owned keys moved — read on 2026-10-04: twelve written, two refused as a later pass's (CARD_OWNERS), and thirteen handed on, each row saying to whom and why.
how_to_change_it: SHRINK ONLY. Read a row, write or refuse what it describes, then run `python3 tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py --retire-ledger`, which takes off the rows whose drift no longer stands and adds none. `--check` is red on drift that is on no row, on a row whose drift no longer stands, and on a rewritten card whose ledgered keys grew. Adding a row by hand is blessing drift nobody has read: don't.

handed_on.why: T-1689 owns these seven cards (its run held the claim when T-2073 read them): the flag was rightly cleared under T-1005 because each card's press_evidence holds a reading that is not a letter list, and the mint sets it back because record() writes it unconditionally. The pass that clears the flag is the pass T-1689 asks to revise the card's name, so the two settle together there.

The re-derivation reads one of two printings of the same name, not more of the corpus: hh_palmer_n_h keeps the 1 July 1835 surname-first reprint and loses the 20 May return (a later, looser bound), and hh_elliot_william and hh_wilson_john lose the 4 March 1834 reprint because the list's count of letters ('Elliot 3', 'Wilson 4') splits it into another person. Writing it would throw a printing away; refused here, settled by the derivation rule T-2076 owns.

The two spellings are two printings of one return (28 January and 4 March 1834) that reach the mint as two candidates. Written on 2026-10-04 and taken back the same day: once the card shows the other spelling, the first stops resolving to it and the mint mints it as a second household (hh_frazer_wm_h, hh_pruvis_joshua, hh_vandine_john — T-2071's re-minted rows are the other face of this pair). Neither spelling is the card's to choose until T-2076 decides how one card reads two printings.
